agree.reason: The reasons are concrete, the email openly says the change breaks what remote hires signed up for, and the partners commit to the same three days, so most staff will probably go along; but the remote hires within two hours get only the commuting money, so some of the ones who stay for remote work may still leave.

honest.reason: Most claims match the brief, but 'projects like these keep a firm our size busy for years' is invented, and 'the people you'd most want to learn from will be there' overstates what five of six project leads coming in actually shows.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are passed on as given: the 30% delay is never turned into months or into what it costs a junior's career, and the email doesn't say that 15 of 46 is about a third or that partners go from one day a week to three.

right_comparison.reason: The email never says what happens if fully remote work continues, such as more lost bids or juniors moving up more slowly, and it doesn't compare the plan with other options like two days or team-based days, so the alternative is only implied.

qualification.reason: The six-month review has a date (around March 2028), but there is no measure or threshold that would change the policy, and the hedge 'we believe part of the reason' names nothing the reader could check.

objections.reason: It answers the 'I was hired as remote' complaint, commuting cost, desk space and the partners' own attendance, but it leaves open whether being in the office would actually have won the hospital bids and why it has to be three days.

fit.reason: It is a clear one-page email with the subject line, meeting time and contacts the brief asked for, sent ahead of Friday's meeting.
